top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) rest on a genuinely new and non-obvious idea: choosing a magic wavelength so the trap light shift cancels, allowing many atoms to be held tightly and interrogated at once. The result is mature, reproduced by independent laboratories with Sr, Yb and Hg at the 10^-18 level, and agrees quantitatively with theory of the systematic shifts. The two-laureate allocation and the citation scope are well matched to the invention and realization of the lattice clock, so an award is clearly preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No direct conflict apparent from profile; as an atomic theorist working on precision atomic structure and with collaborators in the field (e.g. Indelicato), I note only a general subfield proximity, nothing requiring recusal.
